[1685] NURSING AND MIDWIFERY SCIENCES Master's Degree Program

-----

UNIVERSITY: Università degli Studi di Foggia
CURRICULUM: Master's Degree in Nursing and Midwifery
CODE: LM/SNT1
LEVEL: Master's Degree
ACADEMIC YEAR: [Year]
DESCRIPTION: The Master's Degree in Nursing and Midwifery (LM/SNT1) is a national program regulated by Law 2 August 1999, No. 264. Admission is subject to passing a national entrance examination (with 80 multiple-choice questions covering specified thematic areas), with the number of places determined annually by the Ministry of University and Research (MUR) and published in the admission notice on the University of Foggia website. Admission requires possession of one of the following qualifications:
- A three-year university degree enabling practice in a healthcare profession included in the Master's Degree class (SNT/1 class, ex DM 509/99, or L-SNT1 class, DM 270/2004);
- A university diploma enabling practice in a healthcare profession included in the Master's Degree class (SNT/1 class, ex DM 509/99);
- Qualifications enabling practice in a healthcare profession included in the Master's Degree class, as per Law No. 42/1999, or other foreign qualifications recognized as equivalent.

ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Candidates must hold a qualification enabling practice in one of the following professions: Nurse, Pediatric Nurse, Midwife, or an equivalent qualification. Eligible candidates include Italian citizens, EU citizens residing anywhere, and non-EU citizens (as per Article 26 of Law No. 189/2002) holding one of the specified qualifications.

LEARNING OUTCOMES:

Knowledge and Understanding:
- Critical evaluation of professional performance based on practice standards and organizational criteria.
- Identification of personal training needs in relation to problem complexity and management strategies, enabling the design and implementation of a professional improvement plan.
- Autonomous adoption of effective strategies for lifelong learning, utilizing formal and informal learning resources throughout one's professional career, including further training paths.
- Seeking consultation/supervision to enhance competencies through guided critical reflection.
- Critical use of information accessed via information systems, software, and databases to gain new perspectives/data.
- Critical literature review to support problem resolution, analyze available knowledge, develop evidence-based application strategies, and facilitate research dissemination.

Learning Skills:
- Development of lifelong learning capabilities through individual study, project preparation, and thesis work, emphasizing self-directed learning and role modeling.

Assessment Methods for Learning Skills:
- Verification through specific laboratories, evaluating the ability to query databases, access international literature on proposed topics, and present novel research aspects; identifying unresolved issues in various competence areas to guide future research.

Communication Skills:
- Conducting high-complexity interpersonal interviews with users and professionals, adapting strategies to context, problem nature, and objectives, with appropriate listening skills.
- Arguing decisions, positions, and hypotheses in written and oral form using language appropriate for diverse audiences, problems, and contexts.
- Participating in/leading high-complexity negotiations with effective communication, methodological rigor, and convincing arguments respecting others' positions.
- Preventing, managing, and resolving intra- and inter-professional conflicts effectively.
- Leading mono- and multidisciplinary work groups, activating integration strategies (e.g., meetings) to exercise effective leadership.
- Interacting effectively with other healthcare and social professionals in designing and implementing multiprofessional clinical, organizational, educational, and research interventions.
- Planning and managing educational relationships with patients, peers, other healthcare professionals, and students at various training levels.
- Providing consultation for complex relational situations, applying advanced principles and techniques of helping relationships to act as a mentor for aspiring professionals or leader in clinical, organizational, and educational settings.
- Adopting supportive managerial styles to support colleagues in project management, teaching, supervision, negotiation, conflict resolution, and counseling.

Teaching Methods for Communication Skills:
- Development of advanced communication skills (professional, clinical, scientific) through laboratory activities, critical analysis of scientific articles, group discussion of exemplary situations, and subsequent plenary presentations; stage debriefing sessions.

Assessment Methods for Communication Skills:
- Verification at the end of the professional internship period, where the graduate will prepare a written project work for subsequent oral defense.

-----

### Summary of Advanced Nursing Program Competencies  

This program equips nursing professionals with integrated expertise across **four core domains**, emphasizing **evidence-based practice**, **interdisciplinary collaboration**, and **systemic healthcare innovation**. Below are the key competencies structured by domain:  

---

#### **1. Management & Strategic Leadership**  
- **Strategic Planning**: Design community-focused health services by analyzing epidemiological and socio-cultural factors.  
- **Resource Optimization**: Allocate staff based on competency standards and workload demands, balancing efficiency with quality.  
- **Conflict & Crisis Management**: Resolve intra/interprofessional conflicts and navigate high-uncertainty scenarios (e.g., emergencies).  
- **Prevention-Centric Systems**: Shift from reactive to **preventive/regenerative care models**, prioritizing early intervention and holistic resource allocation.  
- **Technology Integration**: Leverage telemedicine and digital tools to enhance service accessibility and continuity (e.g., hospital-territory transitions).  
- **Quality Improvement**: Drive systematic quality/safety initiatives using data-driven decision-making.  

---

#### **2. Advanced Clinical Practice**  
- **Evidence-Based Care**: Develop clinical pathways for complex conditions (e.g., cardiovascular, neurological, oncological, chronic degenerative diseases, palliative care).  
- **Personalized & Multicultural Care**: Address gender-specific needs and cultural contexts in care planning.  
- **Innovative Models**: Implement advanced practices like **case management**, **telemedicine**, and **multidisciplinary collaboration**.  
- **Outcome Evaluation**: Assess clinical outcomes using standardized tools (e.g., *Nursing Minimum Dataset*) and refine care strategies.  
- **Health Promotion**: Design primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention programs for chronic conditions and end-of-life care.  

---

#### **3. Education & Professional Development**  
- **Curriculum Design**: Create tailored educational programs for undergraduate, postgraduate, and lifelong learning (e.g., master’s, certifications).  
- **Mentorship & Supervision**: Guide learners through experiential learning models, fostering autonomy and critical thinking.  
- **Interprofessional Training**: Develop collaborative skills for team-based care and multiprofessional integration.  
- **Evaluation Systems**: Use validated methods to assess learning outcomes, teaching effectiveness, and clinical performance impact.  
- **Community Engagement**: Design educational interventions for families, communities, and self-management of health risks.  

---

#### **4. Research & Innovation**  
- **Methodological Rigor**: Apply quantitative/qualitative research methods to clinical, organizational, and educational contexts.  
- **Problem Identification**: Target gaps in care (e.g., chronic disease management, service organization) for research.  
- **Knowledge Translation**: Bridge research findings to practice, improving clinical, managerial, and educational outcomes.  
- **Interdisciplinary Collaboration**: Partner across fields (e.g., public health, technology) to address complex health challenges.  

---

### **Key Differentiators**  
- **Holistic Integration**: Combines clinical expertise, management acumen, education, and research into a unified framework.  
- **Prevention Focus**: Prioritizes proactive care over reactive treatment (e.g., chronic disease management, palliative care).  
- **Technology & Accessibility**: Uses digital tools (e.g., telemedicine) to enhance care continuity and equity.  
- **Cultural & Gender Sensitivity**: Embeds inclusivity in all care models and educational strategies.  

This program prepares nurses to lead systemic change in modern healthcare, addressing evolving patient needs while advancing professional standards. 🌟

Admission requirements.
Access to the Master's degree program in Sciences and Techniques of Preventive and Adapted Physical Activities is granted to those who have obtained the degree of 'Sciences of Physical Activities and Sports' (L-22) or an equivalent qualification, with knowledge of English or another European Union language at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).
Before enrollment, students will undergo initial assessment tests.
Essential knowledge required for admission:
- Essential scientific-methodological fields for designing, conducting, and evaluating preventive and adapted physical activity programs;
- Teaching methodologies for developing motor skills;
- Teaching methodologies for learning motor skills;
- Teaching methodologies for recovery and development of motor skills in adulthood and old age;
- Teaching methodologies for recovery and development of motor skills in disabled subjects;
- Methodologies for injury prevention;
- Motor assessment methodologies;
- Knowledge of systems and apparatus responsible for movement;
- Biochemical and physiological modifications of systems and apparatus induced by physical exercise;
- Fundamentals of sociology;
- Scientific foundations of developmental psychology;
- Fundamentals of learning pedagogy;
- Knowledge of major organic pathological conditions linked to sedentary lifestyles.
Learning abilities.
Graduates in Sciences and Techniques of Preventive and Adapted Physical Activities must be able to identify essential knowledge from each course to expand content and establish interdisciplinary relationships; internship and thesis preparation will enable students to identify bibliographic references and databases for continuous training and updating, and to continue personal formation on interdisciplinary topics through 'in-person' and 'distance' methodologies.
This ability is assessed in all examination sessions and more comprehensively during the final exam.
Communication skills.
Graduates in Sciences and Techniques of Preventive and Adapted Physical Activities must be able to:
- Differentiate and adapt teaching communication according to different age groups and motor and educational needs;
- Use technical and technological tools for analyzing teacher-student interactions, observing socio-emotional behaviors, and verifying motor learning;
- Appropriately disseminate results of applied scientific research protocols aimed at promoting physically active lifestyles;
- Prepare reports on completed training processes.
Communication skills will also be developed during seminar activities, internships, and specifically assessed during the final exam.

**Course Description: Adapted Physical Activities and Sports**  

The study program trains students with adequate cultural and operational skills for the management and evaluation of individual and group motor activities with educational, recreational, and sporting characteristics, aimed at maintaining psychophysical well-being through the promotion of active lifestyles for different age groups and educational needs.  

The course aims to analyze the formative value and methodological processes related to motor teaching and learning for individuals of varying ages and those with special educational needs. The didactic regulations and course offerings will allow students to pursue training paths that include an appropriate number of credits in related and complementary fields not already characteristic of the program.  

**Training Objectives:**  
- Recognize the epistemological frameworks from which to derive the methodologies of adapted physical activities.  
- Analyze the contribution of biomedical sciences to preventive and adapted physical activities.  
- Analyze the contribution of educational and social sciences to preventive and adapted physical activities.  
- Identify the educational needs of diverse user groups (children, people with disabilities, elderly individuals, adults, recreational athletes, socially excluded individuals, etc.).  
- Design, implement, and evaluate adapted physical activity programs for injury prevention and rehabilitation.  
- Define objectives for "adapted" physical activity tailored to different age groups and cognitive, emotional, social, and motor needs.  
- Assess the learning process of preventive and adapted physical activities through various methods, including systematic observation, testing, and the use of instruments and equipment.  

The training program aims to equip students with knowledge and skills adapted to the proposal and implementation of methodological innovations in physical and sports activities for different life stages and individuals affected by congenital or acquired physical and mental conditions with chronic progression and impact on social participation.  

The course is designed to acquire knowledge and understanding of anatomical, biochemical, physiological, and pathophysiological mechanisms of major multifactorial diseases requiring stabilization, necessary for designing and implementing "adapted" physical activities aimed at maintaining health conditions and preventing organic and psychological complications. Methodological focus is placed on postural defects, metabolic syndromes, chronic cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, oncological diseases, neurological diseases, and the consequences of their treatments, to develop the ability to design specific motor and sports interventions for these groups.  

The program includes theoretical-practical teaching modules focused on designing, implementing, and evaluating motor activities for developmental, adult, and elderly populations, as well as for individuals with disabilities and for recreational and sporting purposes.  

**Course Structure:**  
- **Two-Year Program (Biennium):** Includes integrated courses (corso integrato) led by the principal instructor (docente titolare).  
- **Practical Training (Tirocinio Formativo e di Orientamento):** Conducted at affiliated gyms (palestre convenzionate) under the supervision of a tutor.  
- **Credits (CFU):** The program includes a specified number of credits (CFU) for each course component.  

**Teaching Methods:**  
- Theoretical instruction combined with practical application.  
- Systematic observation and assessment of motor learning processes.  
- Use of specialized equipment and testing methods.  
- Collaboration with affiliated institutions for practical training.  

**Target Audience:**  
Students seeking expertise in designing and managing adapted physical activities for diverse populations, including those with disabilities, chronic conditions, or special educational needs.  

**Outcome:**  
Graduates will be qualified to work in educational, therapeutic, and recreational settings, promoting inclusive physical activity programs that enhance quality of life and social inclusion. The program emphasizes evidence-based methodologies, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the development of innovative approaches to meet the evolving needs of diverse populations.

### **Riassunto del Corso di Laurea Magistrale in "Scienze delle Professioni Sanitarie Tecniche Diagnostiche"**  
*(Università di Foggia)*  

#### **Struttura Generale**  
- **Durata**: 2 anni (120 CFU totali).  
- **CFU**:  
  - **1 CFU** = 25 ore di lavoro studentesco (8 ore lezione + 17 ore studio individuale per lezioni; 15 ore laboratorio + 10 ore studio per attività non formali; 25 ore tirocinio per attività professionalizzanti).  
  - **30 CFU** dedicati a **attività professionalizzanti** (tirocinio presso strutture sanitarie partner).  

---

#### **Curriculum**  
**Primo Anno**: *Fondamenti per la gestione e l’etica professionale*  
- **Diritto pubblico, privato e medicina legale** (gestione atti amministrativi).  
- **Prevenzione rischi sanitari** negli ambienti lavorativi.  
- **Etica professionale** e deontologia.  
- **Strumenti informatici** per gestione dati e ricerca.  
- **Psicologia e pedagogia** per interazioni con personale e pazienti.  
- **Metodologie didattiche** per comunicazione e formazione.  

**Secondo Anno**: *Specializzazione inagnostica e management*  
- **Logiche aziendali** e ottimizzazione risorse sanitarie.  
- **Strumenti di management** per strutture complesse.  
- **Applicazione ricerca** al miglioramento assistenziale.  
- **Metodologie avanzate** per interventi diagnostici/assistenziali.  
- **Progettazione formativa** per aggiornamento professionale.  

---

#### **Punti di Forza**  
1. **Tirocinio pratico** (30 CFU) presso:  
   - Policlinico Universitario di Foggia.  
   - Ospedale di Barletta.  
   - IRCS Casa del sollievo della Sofferenza (San Giovanni Rotondo).  
2. **Approccio integrato**:  
   - Combinazione di **management**, **ricerca**, **innovazione** e **formazione**.  
   - Focus su **qualità dei servizi** e **miglioramento continuo** (es. analisi critica processi tecnico-assistenziali).  
3. **Qualità garantita**:  
   - Monitoraggio costante da parte del **Gruppo di Assicurazione della Qualità** (4 docenti + 1 studente + rappresentante amministrativo).  
4. **Metodi didattici**:  
   - Lezioni frontali, seminari, gruppi di discussione, laboratori.  
   - Valutazione tramite esami scritti/orali, prove in itinere e elaborati.  

---

#### **Obiettivi Formativi**  
- Formare professionisti in grado di:  
  - Gestire strutture sanitarie complesse con **approccio manageriale**.  
  - Applicare **risultati di ricerca** per migliorare l’assistenza.  
  - Progettare **percorsi formativi** per il personale tecnico-diagnostico.  
  - Interagire efficacemente con pazienti, familiari e team multidisciplinari.  

---

#### **Differenziali**  
- **Partnership con strutture ospedaliere** per tirocini reali.  
- **Focus su innovazione e ricerca** integrata nella pratica clinica.  
- **Attenzione all’etica e alla comunicazione** (strumenti psicopedagogici).  

Questo corso si distingue per l’equilibrio tra **competenze tecniche**, **gestione organizzativa** e **sviluppo professionale continuo**, preparando gli studenti a ruoli di leadership nel settore sanitario.

### **Riassunto del Programma di Laurea Magistrale in Odontoiatria e Protesi Dentaria (Classe LM-46)**  
**Durata:** 6 anni (ciclo unico), abilitante all'esercizio della professione di odontoiatra.  

---

#### **Struttura del Corso**  
1. **Primo Triennio (Anni 1-3):**  
   - Fondamenti biologici, strutturali e funzionali del corpo umano.  
   - Metodologia scientifica, relazione medico-paziente e principi etici.  
   - Introduzione al metodo diagnostico per problemi oro-dentali.  

2. **Secondo Triennio (Anni 4-6):**  
   - Discipline specialistiche: chirurgia orale, odontoiatria restaurativa, endodonzia, implantologia, parodontologia, ortodonzia, odontoiatria pediatrica, patologia orale e protesi.  
   - **Anno 5:** Introduzione a patologia maxillo-facciale e implantologia.  
   - **Anno 6:** Focus su cure cliniche avanzate, con tirocinio integrato.  

---

#### **Tirocinio Pratico-Valutativo (TPV)**  
- **Obiettivo:** Acquisire competenze pratiche come **primo operatore** in ambito preventivo, diagnostico e terapeutico.  
- **Crediti (CFU):**  
  - **Totale:** 90 CFU (obbligatori per l'abilitazione).  
  - **30 CFU** come primo operatore (20 ore/CFU in strutture universitarie o SSN, con convenzione).  
  - **Fino al 30%** (max 27 CFU) può essere svolto **all'anno 5**, il resto all'anno 6.  
- **Discipline coperte:** Chirurgia orale, endodonzia, implantologia, parodontologia, odontoiatria pediatrica, ecc.  

---

#### **Esame Finale**  
1. **Prova Pratica Valutativa (PPV):**  
   - Discussione di **3 casi clinici multidisciplinari** trattati come primo operatore durante il TPV.  
   - **Obiettivo:** Verificare competenze pratiche per l'abilitazione.  
   - **Requisito:** Superamento della PPV **prima** della discussione della tesi.  
2. **Tesi di Laurea:**  
   - Discussione dopo il superamento della PPV.  

---

#### **Requisiti Obbligatori**  
- **Lingua:** Fluente in **almeno una lingua UE** (oltre all'italiano), con lessico tecnico.  
- **Normativa:** Rispetto delle norme medico-legali ed etiche italiane e UE.  
- **Approccio olistico:** Integrazione tra salute orale, ambiente fisico/sociale e patologie sistemiche.  

---

#### **Basi Legali**  
- **Legge 163/2021** e **Decreto Ministeriale 653/2022**.  
- L'esame finale con PPV è **obbligatorio** per ottenere l'abilitazione professionale.  

---

#### **Punti Chiave**  
- **Focus su esperienza pratica:** Il 30% dei CFU del TPV richiede l'operatività diretta come primo operatore.  
- **Integrazione teoria-pratica:** Tirocini strutturati in tutte le specialità dentali.  
- **Preparazione professionale:** Adatto per l'esercizio in ambito pubblico (SSN) o privato.  

> **Nota:** Il programma non è solo accademico, ma è progettato per formare professionisti pronti a operare in contesti clinici complessi, con attenzione alla sicurezza e all'etica.  

---  
*Fonte: Testo ufficiale del DM 653/2022 e Legge 163/2021.*

### Concise Summary: Medical and Surgical Master's Degree (Italy)  

**Program Structure**  
- **Duration**: 6 years (360 CFUs total).  
- **Practical Training**: Minimum 60 CFUs dedicated to clinical practice, internships, and professional skill development.  
- **CFU Breakdown**:  
  - 1 CFU = 25 hours (lectures, labs, or self-directed study).  
  - Professional CFUs (tutoring/practicals) align with 25 hours of direct engagement.  

**Key Objectives**  
- **Mission**: Integrate **biomedical** (disease-focused) and **psychosocial** (holistic patient care) approaches, emphasizing the patient as a whole (body, mind, social context).  
- **Learning Outcomes**:  
  - Multidisciplinary, preventive, and community-oriented healthcare.  
  - Clinical problem-solving, communication, teamwork, and health economics.  
  - Alignment with **Dublin Descriptors**, **IIME**, and **TUNING Project** standards.  
- **Teaching Method**:  
  - Early patient contact, problem-based learning, and vertical/horizontal integration of basic sciences, clinical practice, and humanities.  

**Professional Requirements**  
- **Mandatory for**:  
  - Practicing as a physician (all specialties).  
  - Entry into **Specialization Schools** (e.g., surgery, pediatrics) and **General Medicine Training**.  
- **Competencies**:  
  - Clinical evaluation, preventive care, patient communication, community health intervention, and ethical decision-making.  

**Academic Support**  
- **OFA (Additional Educational Obligation)**:  
  - Required for students lacking foundational knowledge (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Math, Reasoning).  
  - Must be completed by **October 31** of the following academic year via supplementary courses/exams.  
  - Failure to complete OFA restricts enrollment in exams until resolved.  

**Unique Focus**  
- **Holistic Care**: Prioritizes patient-centered care over disease-centric treatment.  
- **Interdisciplinary Approach**: Combines biomedical science, clinical practice, and social context.  

This program prepares graduates for **entry-level medical practice** with a strong emphasis on **ethical, preventive, and community-focused healthcare**.

[1683] CLINICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL BIOLOGY Master's Degree Course English

-----

The Master's program in Clinical and Experimental Biology is designed to equip students with advanced scientific knowledge and practical skills for research and professional roles in biomedical fields. Key features include:

**Admission Requirements:**  
- A bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences (L-13) or Biotechnology (L-2) under Italian regulations (D.M. 270/04), or an equivalent international degree.  
- Specific credit requirements:  
  - 12 CFU in non-biological basic sciences (mathematics, physics, informatics).  
  - 12 CFU in non-biological chemistry.  
  - 40 CFU in designated biological/medical disciplines (e.g., BIO/01–BIO/19, MED/03–MED/42).  
- English proficiency at B2 level (verified via prior studies or certification).  

**Program Structure:**  
- **Thesis Requirement:** A minimum 8-month internship in a university or external lab, culminating in a 35-credit thesis written in English. The thesis must follow scientific standards (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).  
- **Learning Outcomes:** Graduates develop:  
  - Autonomous learning skills for continuous professional development.  
  - Ability to critically evaluate research, design experiments, and use advanced scientific databases.  
  - Strong communication skills in English for presenting research (oral/written) in international contexts.  
  - Competence in interdisciplinary teamwork and laboratory management.  

**Assessment:**  
- Continuous evaluation through exams, project work, seminars, and thesis defense.  
- Final thesis defense before a committee, assessing scientific writing, presentation, and critical thinking.  

**International Students:**  
- May undergo a tailored admission test and require a positive evaluation for eligibility.  
- Exempt from additional proficiency tests if they pass the initial assessment.  

This program prepares students for further studies (PhD, master’s) or careers in research, biotechnology, and healthcare, emphasizing global collaboration and evidence-based practice.

-----

**Summary of the Master's Program in Clinical and Experimental Biology**  

This Master’s program (aligned with Italian academic classification **LM-06**) is designed to equip students with advanced, practical expertise in **biomedical and biomolecular sciences**, preparing them for careers in research, healthcare, industry, and public health. The curriculum emphasizes **interdisciplinary approaches** to address complex biological challenges, integrating theoretical knowledge with hands-on experimental skills.  

---

### **Key Features**  
1. **Dual Curriculum Tracks**:  
   - **Biomedical Focus**: Prepares students for healthcare roles (e.g., clinical research, diagnostics) with courses in *Pathology, Immunology, Microbiology, and Pharmacology*.  
   - **Applied Biology Focus**: Centers on *cellular and molecular analysis*, ideal for industry or biotech roles (e.g., drug development, genetic engineering).  

2. **Core Disciplines**:  
   - Biochemistry, Cell & Molecular Biology, Human Anatomy, Physiology, Pathology, Immunology, Microbiology, and Pharmacology.  
   - Strong emphasis on **biomedical sciences** (unlike other LM-06 programs), with minimal overlap in non-biomedical fields.  

3. **Innovative Teaching Methods**:  
   - **Problem-Based Learning (PBL)**: Students analyze scientific literature and discuss cutting-edge research in seminars.  
   - **Lab-Driven Training**: Combines lectures with hands-on experiments, data analysis, and critical evaluation of methodologies.  
   - **International Collaboration**: Opportunities for study abroad (EU/non-EU) via university partnerships.  

4. **Practical Components**:  
   - **Mandatory Internships**: In industry, hospitals, or research labs to gain real-world experience.  
   - **Thesis Project**: Original research in biomedical or biomolecular fields, fostering scientific independence and managerial skills.  
   - **Microcredentials**: Flexible, modular courses (e.g., specialized technical skills) aligned with global job market demands.  

5. **Language & Skills**:  
   - **Fluency in English** (scientific terminology) required for global collaboration.  
   - Training in **data analysis tools** and **scientific communication**.  

---

### **Career Pathways**  
Graduates are prepared for roles in:  
- **Healthcare**: Clinical research, diagnostics, hospital labs.  
- **Industry**: Biotech, pharmaceuticals, genetic engineering.  
- **Research**: Universities, public/private research institutions.  
- **Public Health**: Policy development, health technology innovation.  

---

### **Program Structure**  
- **Core Courses**: Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Pathology, Immunology, etc.  
- **Electives**: Tailored to biomedical or applied tracks (e.g., advanced genomics, drug design).  
- **Flexible Credits**: "Free-choice" credits for interdisciplinary modules (e.g., AI in biomedicine) or international exchanges.  
- **Department**: Delivered by the **Department of Clinical and Experimental Medicine** at the **Biomedical Campus**, featuring modern lab facilities.  

---

### **Next Steps**  
- **Further Studies**: Prepares students for **PhD programs**, **specialization schools**, or **Master’s in Advanced Biotechnology**.  
- **Global Readiness**: International collaborations and English proficiency ensure competitiveness in global markets.  

This program stands out for its **integration of theory, hands-on research, and industry-aligned training**, positioning graduates to lead innovation in biomedicine and life sciences.

Roles President GIUSEPPE GUGLIELMI Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
MEDICAL RADIOLOGY TECHNICIAN Graduates in Medical Radiology Techniques work professionally in healthcare facilities, public or private, under employment or as self-employed professionals; they contribute to the training of support staff and directly participate in professional updating.
Final exam characteristics.
The characteristics of the final exam are those indicated in art. 7, paragraph 4 of D.M. 19.02.2009 n.119. The degree is obtained by passing a final exam consisting of the writing and discussion of a written paper on a theoretical-practical topic. It is preceded by a professional exam, enabling the profession of Medical Radiology Technician for Imaging and Radiotherapy, demonstrating skills related to professional practice, which can be carried out as a simulated practical exam. Papers may also be written in a foreign language previously agreed upon. The final exam has the value of a State Exam enabling professional practice.
Required knowledge for access.
Candidates who possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable, in accordance with art. 6, paragraph 1 of D.M. 22/10/2004, n. 270, may be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Medical Radiology, Imaging and Radiotherapy. Admission to the Bachelor's Degree course takes place according to modalities defined by the Ministry of Education, Universities and Research, and currently consists of a written test covering topics in Logic and General Culture, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics.
Learning abilities.
Graduates in Medical Radiology, Imaging and Radiotherapy must:
- be able to learn in an integrated and continuous manner all key fundamental aspects of the discipline, using integrated multidisciplinary knowledge acquired;
- be able to learn to communicate with medical physicists to discuss quality control issues;
- be able to learn to communicate with radiologists, nuclear medicine physicians, radiotherapists and other specialists to collaborate effectively in implementing technical procedures within their competence;
- be able to learn to communicate with administrative staff, other radiology technicians, health professionals, radiologists, nuclear medicine physicians, radiotherapists and other specialists to best organize work in departments;
- be able to learn to communicate with technical staff for radiological equipment and radiological hospital information systems to resolve technical problems and malfunctions;
- be able to learn to communicate with citizens who rely on their professionalism to clearly and understandably explain the radiological procedure they will undergo, ensuring their cooperation while respecting their rights.
These abilities will be acquired and verified through meetings with patients, tutors and assistants, promoting active student participation and multidisciplinary team work and final reports.

-----

### Summary of the **"Tecniche Sanitarie di Radiologia Medica" (Medical Radiology Technical Sciences) Program**  

#### **Program Overview**  
This undergraduate program prepares graduates to become **Medical Radiology Technicians** (Tecnico Sanitario di Radiologia Medica), a profession immediately recognized and authorized under **Italian Law (D.M. 26 September 1994, n. 746)**. Graduates are qualified to work autonomously or collaboratively in public/private healthcare settings, performing radiological procedures, managing imaging equipment, and ensuring radiation safety. The program integrates **theoretical knowledge**, **practical skills**, and **professional competencies** to meet modern healthcare demands.  

---

#### **Key Legal and Professional Authorization**  
- The degree is **immediately abilitative** (no additional exams required) for the profession.  
- Graduates operate under **medical prescriptions** and comply with **radiation protection regulations** (e.g., Law 31 January 1983, n. 25).  
- Responsibilities include:  
  - Performing diagnostic/therapeutic procedures (X-ray, CT, MRI, nuclear medicine, radiotherapy).  
  - Ensuring equipment safety and quality control.  
  - Collaborating with radiologists, nuclear medicine physicians, and medical physicists.  
  - Contributing to healthcare management and staff training.  

---

#### **Core Competencies Developed**  
1. **Technical Expertise**:  
   - Radiodiagnostic imaging (CT, MRI, nuclear medicine, neuroradiology).  
   - Radiotherapy and brachytherapy.  
   - Radiation protection and dosimetry.  
   - Medical physics and biomedical instrumentation.  
2. **Clinical and Safety Skills**:  
   - Emergency response and first aid.  
   - Radiation safety protocols and quality assurance.  
3. **Soft Skills & Professional Conduct**:  
   - Patient communication and psychological support (via human sciences/psychopedagogy).  
   - Team collaboration in multidisciplinary healthcare teams.  
4. **Management & Legal Knowledge**:  
   - Healthcare economics, public health, and medical-legal aspects.  
   - Healthcare management and administrative protocols.  

---

#### **Curriculum Structure**  
- **Theoretical Courses**:  
  - Anatomy, physiology, and biomedical sciences.  
  - Medical statistics, informatics, and electrical/electronic measurements.  
  - Radioprotection, radiation physics, and imaging techniques.  
- **Practical Training**:  
  - **Laboratories** (e.g., MED/50 specialized labs for hands-on radiology practice).  
  - **Clinical internships** in radiology, radiotherapy, and nuclear medicine departments.  
- **Additional Modules**:  
  - English for scientific communication.  
  - Public health, prevention, and healthcare management.  
  - Seminars on emerging trends in radiology.  

---

#### **Professional Roles Post-Graduation**  
Graduates work in:  
- **Public/private hospitals** (radiology departments, radiotherapy units).  
- **Diagnostic imaging centers** and **oncology clinics**.  
- **Radiation safety roles** (e.g., quality control, dosimetry).  
- **Freelance or institutional positions** (e.g., equipment management, training).  

---

#### **Unique Features**  
- **Holistic Approach**: Combines technical, clinical, legal, and managerial training.  
- **Radiation Safety Focus**: Mandatory training in radioprotection (aligned with EU standards).  
- **Modern Relevance**: Covers advanced techniques (e.g., AI in imaging, 3D reconstruction).  
- **Global Readiness**: Emphasis on **scientific English** for international collaboration.  

---

#### **Why This Program Stands Out**  
Unlike purely technical programs, it ensures graduates are **versatile professionals** capable of adapting to evolving healthcare technologies while prioritizing **patient safety**, **ethical practice**, and **interdisciplinary teamwork**. The curriculum aligns with **Italian and European healthcare standards**, preparing students for both clinical roles and leadership in radiology departments.  

*Note: Admission requires a competitive entrance exam (test di ammissione), with priority given to candidates selecting "prima opzione" (first choice) in the application process.*  

---  
This program is a **comprehensive pathway** to a high-demand healthcare profession, blending innovation, safety, and patient-centered care. Graduates are equipped to contribute meaningfully to diagnostic accuracy, treatment efficacy, and radiation safety in modern medicine. 🏥🔬💡

Information Management

### **Biomedical Laboratory Technician Degree Program: Summary**  
This program prepares graduates to work as **Biomedical Laboratory Technicians** (Tecnico sanitario di laboratorio biomedico), equipping them with the technical, analytical, and interpersonal skills required for modern laboratory environments. Below is a structured overview of the program’s core components:

---

#### **1. Professional Role & Core Competencies**  
Graduates:  
- Operate in **public/private accredited laboratories**, working under supervision or independently.  
- **Manage the entire analytical process**, from pre-analytical phase (sample collection, handling) to post-analytical reporting.  
- Specialize in key areas:  
  - *Clinical Biochemistry, Microbiology, Parasitology, Virology, Immunology, Hematology, Cytology, Histopathology, Medical Genetics*.  
- Ensure **quality control** (e.g., calibration, equipment maintenance, validation of protocols) and **safety compliance** (risk management, radioprotection).  
- Collaborate with **senior laboratory staff** and interdisciplinary teams to optimize diagnostic/production workflows.  
- Apply **scientific progress** to improve efficiency (e.g., adopting new technologies, cost analysis).  

---

#### **2. Work Context & Responsibilities**  
- **Pre-analytical phase**: Critical for diagnostic accuracy (e.g., sample integrity, patient identification).  
- **Analytical phase**: Execute tests in specialized labs (e.g., molecular diagnostics, microbiological cultures).  
- **Post-analytical phase**: Verify results against quality standards, report findings, and troubleshoot errors.  
- **Ethical & legal compliance**: Adhere to medical-legal standards, patient confidentiality, and laboratory regulations.  
- **Continuous improvement**: Contribute to staff training, quality assurance, and research.  

---

#### **3. Educational Objectives**  
The program focuses on **theoretical-practical integration** across:  
- **Core disciplines**:  
  - Clinical pathology, molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry, hematology.  
  - Medical ethics, legal frameworks (e.g., medical-legal implications), and public health.  
- **Supporting disciplines**:  
  - Human anatomy/physiology, pharmacology, medical statistics, bioengineering.  
  - *Management skills*: Healthcare economics, organizational behavior, and hospital administration.  
- **Soft skills**:  
  - Communication (patient interaction, teamwork), critical thinking, and adaptability in dynamic work environments.  

---

#### **4. Curriculum Structure**  
| **Category**               | **Key Components**                                                                 |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Core Courses**           | Clinical diagnostics, microbiology, molecular biology, histopathology, quality management. |
| **Basic Courses**          | Human biology, pharmacology, medical physics, statistics, bioengineering.        |
| **Professional Labs (MED/46)** | Hands-on training in biomedical lab techniques (e.g., PCR, serology, cytology). |
| **Additional Elements**    | - **English for Science**: Technical terminology and scientific literature. <br> - **Seminars**: Emerging trends (e.g., AI in diagnostics, genomics). <br> - **Mandatory Internship**: 6–12 months in accredited labs (tirocinio abilitante). |

---

#### **5. Unique Program Features**  
- **Interdisciplinary focus**: Bridges clinical science, technology, and healthcare management.  
- **Quality & safety emphasis**: Training in ISO standards, risk assessment, and equipment validation.  
- **Career readiness**: Prepares graduates for roles in hospitals, research labs, diagnostic centers, and public health agencies.  
- **Global relevance**: English proficiency and exposure to international standards (e.g., CLIA, ISO 15189).  

---

#### **6. Professional Outcomes**  
Graduates are qualified to:  
- Perform **diagnostic tests** (e.g., blood analysis, genetic screening, pathogen detection).  
- **Lead quality assurance** initiatives and contribute to laboratory accreditation.  
- **Collaborate across specialties** (e.g., oncology, infectious disease) to support patient care.  
- **Pursue advanced roles** in research, management, or specialized diagnostics (e.g., molecular pathology).  

---

This program ensures graduates are **technically proficient, ethically grounded, and adaptable** to evolving healthcare demands, aligning with global standards for biomedical laboratory practice.

**Sintesi del Corso di Laurea in Scienze Motorie**  
*Programma triennale in conformità al Regolamento Didattico e al Decreto MIUR 270/2004*

---

### **Struttura del Corso**  
Il corso si articola in **tre anni** (180 CFU), con un approccio **multidisciplinare** che integra teoria e pratica. Le attività didattiche sono organizzate in quattro macro-aree:  
1. **Tecnico-motoria**: Discipline sportive, allenamento, programmazione didattica.  
2. **Biomedica**: Salute, funzioni motorie, sviluppo nell’età evolutiva.  
3. **Psicopedagogia**: Relazioni tra motorietà, cognizione ed emotività.  
4. **Giuridica**: Normativa sportiva e regolamenti disciplinari.  

---

### **Tirocinio Formativo (Punto Chiave)**  
- **Obiettivi**:  
  - Collegare teoria e pratica (didattica, organizzazione, ricerca).  
  - Garantire continuità tra insegnamenti e ambiti professionali.  
  - Favorire l’interazione università-mercato del lavoro.  
- **Attività previste**:  
  - Programmazione didattica per diverse fasce d’età.  
  - Osservazione interazioni insegnante-allievo.  
  - Valutazione motoria e socio-affettiva con strumenti standardizzati.  
  - Organizzazione di manifestazioni sportive.  
  - Analisi di videoriprese per migliorare l’insegnamento.  
- **Durata**: Ore dedicate sufficienti a consolidare competenze in contesti reali (convenzioni con enti esterni).  

---

### **Obiettivi Formativi Specifici**  
Gli studenti acquisiranno:  
- **Conoscenze scientifiche** su motorietà, salute e sviluppo psicofisico.  
- **Competenze applicative**: progettazione di percorsi motori adattati a handicap, allenamento, organizzazione di eventi.  
- **Metodo critico**: confronto con il mondo professionale internazionale e aggiornamento continuo.  
- **Lingua inglese e informatica**: requisiti essenziali per sbocchi occupazionali.  

---

### **Sbocchi Professionali**  
Il percorso prepara a ruoli in ambito **pubblico e privato**, tra cui:  
- Allenatore sportivo e preparatore fisico.  
- Coordinatore di impianti sportivi e strutture ricreative.  
- Organizzatore di manifestazioni sportive.  
- Educatore motorio per diverse fasce d’età (infanzia, anziani, disabili).  

---

### **Flessibilità e Innovazione**  
- **Corsi a scelta libera**: Possibilità di integrare discipline affini (es. psicologia, gestione aziendale).  
- **Approccio pratico**: Attività in gruppo, laboratori, e collaborazione con il territorio.  
- **Conformità normativa**: Il corso rispetta il Decreto MIUR 270/2004, garantendo riconoscimento nazionale.  

---

### **Perché Scegliere Questo Corso?**  
- **Equilibrio teoria-pratica**: Il tirocinio è parte integrante, non opzionale.  
- **Ampia versatilità**: Competenze trasversali per adattarsi a diversi settori (sport, salute, istruzione).  
- **Sbocchi garantiti**: Il mercato richiede professionisti formati su aspetti tecnici, biomedici e psicopedagogici.  

*Il corso si distingue per l’attenzione alla personalizzazione delle attività motorie e alla preparazione a contesti reali, preparando gli studenti a diventare professionisti completi nel settore motorio e sportivo.*

Roles President ROSELLA SCRIMA Program, Texts, and Objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
JUNIOR BIOLOGIST For the holder of a first-level degree in Biological Sciences, registration in Section B of the National Order of Biologists (as Junior Biologist) is required, following the successful completion of the corresponding State Exam.
The Junior Biologist can be employed in the workforce as an employee or as a self-employed professional in various fields of application of biological disciplines, such as:
- Public and private research laboratories and institutions for analysis in various fields of biology operating in sectors such as biotechnology, environmental science, and health;
- Public and private research laboratories and institutions for analysis in various fields of biology operating in sectors such as biotechnology, environmental science, and health.
These competencies will be acquired primarily through specific exercises related to some courses, during the internship, preparation of the final thesis, and the period of the final exam.

Learning Objectives
Acquisition of adequate skills and knowledge to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy and to develop and deepen further competencies in the fields of biology and related areas, with reference to: consultation of bibliographic material, consultation of databases and other online information, basic knowledge tools for continuous updating of knowledge. These competencies will be acquired mainly during specific exercises related to some courses, during the internship, preparation of the final thesis, and the period of the final exam.

Communication Skills
Communication skills in terms of acquisition of adequate competencies and tools for written and oral communication with reference to: communication in Italian and foreign language (English) in written and oral form; IT skills, data processing and presentation; ability to work in a group; transmission and dissemination of information on current biological and biotechnological topics. Such competencies will be acquired through attendance at lectures, exercises, and seminars, also referring to additional training activities and the possibility of participating in Erasmus programs. Verification will be carried out through the preparation of reports, group work, and/or tests.

-----

Ecco una sintesi chiara e strutturata delle informazioni principali riguardo al **Corso di Laurea in Scienze Biologiche** (L-13) e del ruolo del **Biologo Junior**, basata sul testo fornito:

---

### **Profilo del Corso di Laurea**
- **Durata e CFU**: 3 anni, **180 CFU** totali.
- **Struttura**: Due curricula:
  1. **Generale** (180 CFU).
  2. **Ecologico-Ambientale** (180 CFU).
- **Modalità didattica**: **Mista** (in presenza + e-learning tramite piattaforma CEA).
- **Obiettivo formativo**: Preparare laureati con competenze metodologiche e operative per:
  - Lavorare in ambito biologico, ambientale, biotecnologico.
  - Accedere a corsi di laurea magistrale senza debiti.
  - Inserirsi direttamente nel mondo del lavoro.

---

### **Competenze Richieste per il "Biologo Junior"**
Il laureato triennale può svolgere attività tecniche e operative in contesti come:
1. **Ricerca e monitoraggio**: Analisi biologiche, ambientali, di qualità (acqua, aria, suolo, alimenti).
2. **Biotecnologie e biomedicina**: Procedure analitiche e strumentali (es. diagnosi, ricerca).
3. **Controllo qualità**: In ambito chimico-fisico, microbiologico, farmacologico, genetico.
4. **Collaborazione**: Con medici, biologi magistrali, ingegneri, chimici, veterinari.

**Requisiti chiave**:
- Capacità di operare con autonomia e integrarsi in team.
- Conoscenza di almeno una lingua UE (oltre all’italiano).
- Competenze nella comunicazione scritta/orale e gestione informazioni.
- Aggiornamento continuo tramite strumenti digitali.

---

### **Struttura del Corso**
| **Componente**               | **CFU** | **Dettagli**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tirocinio formativo**      | 10      | Attività presso aziende, pubblica amministrazione, laboratori.               |
| **Lingua straniera (inglese)**| 5       | Obbligatorio per la comunicazione scientifica.                              |
| **Prova finale**             | 3       | Relazione scritta su tema specifico collegato ai corsi.                     |
| **Insegnamenti obbligatori**  | 162     | Matematica, Fisica, Chimica, Biologia molecolare, Ecologia, Bioetica, ecc. |
| **Insegnamenti a scelta**     | Vari    | Per approfondimenti personalizzati (es. biotecnologie, ecologia avanzata).  |

---

### **Insegnamenti Chiave**
- **Misti (in presenza + e-learning)**: Matematica, Fisica, Informatica, Inglese, Ecologia, Bioetica, Sicurezza in laboratorio.
- **Laboratori**: Attività pratiche integrate nei corsi o in laboratori convenzionati.
- **Allineamento nazionale**: Rispetta le linee guida **CBUI** (Collegio dei Biologi delle Università Italiane) e la **Tabella Tuning**.

---

### **Opportunità di Lavoro**
Il **Biologo Junior** può lavorare in:
- Laboratori di analisi (ambiente, alimentare, sanitario).
- Aziende biotecnologiche e farmaceutiche.
- Pubblica amministrazione (controllo qualità, tutela ambientale).
- Strutture di ricerca (supporto a progetti scientifici).

> **Nota**: Il titolo "Biologo Junior" non è ufficiale, ma indica il ruolo professionale accessibile con la laurea triennale (differente dal "Biologo Magistrale", richiesto per ruoli più avanzati).

---

### **Perché Scegliere Questo Corso?**
- **Flessibilità**: Modalità mista per studenti lavoratori, fuori sede o con disabilità.
- **Preparazione pratica**: Tirocinio obbligatorio e laboratori.
- **Accesso a percorsi futuri**: Facilità nell’accesso a lauree magistrali (es. Biologia Molecolare, Ecologia).
- **Riconoscimento nazionale**: Allineamento alle linee guida CBUI e Tuning.

---

Se hai bisogno di approfondire un aspetto specifico (es. dettagli sul tirocinio, confronto con altri corsi, o requisiti per l’accesso), fammelo sapere! 😊

COURSE: [1686] LOGOPEDICS (ENTITLING TO THE HEALTH PROFESSION OF SPEECH THERAPIST)
TYPE: COURSE
CURRICULUM: CURRICULUM
SECTION: Syllabus, texts and objectives
URL: https://unifg.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10733

Syllabus, texts and objectives Professional status conferred by the degree.
Speech Therapist I graduates in Logopedics carry out their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in dependent or self-employed status. They may find employment in facilities of the national and regional health services; in private facilities accredited and contracted with the SSN; in rehabilitation clinics, centers and facilities; in Sanitary Assistance Residences; at patients' homes; in thermal resorts; in medical and/or multi-specialty outpatient clinics; in service cooperatives. Current regulations permit the exercise of self-employed activities in individual or associated professional offices. They may carry out study and research activities, teaching, and support for all activities requiring specific professional expertise.
Final exam characteristics.
The degree in Logopedics is obtained by passing a final exam consisting of the writing and discussion of a written paper on a theoretical-practical topic. It is preceded by a professional exam, entitling to the profession of Speech Therapist, demonstrating skills related to clinical practice through a simulated practical test. Papers may also be written in a foreign language previously agreed upon. The final exam has the value of a State Exam entitling to professional practice.
Required knowledge for admission.
To be admitted to the degree course in Logopedics, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree, in accordance with Ministerial Decree No. 270 of 22 October 2004. Admission to the course is nationally regulated in accordance with Law No. 264 of 2 August 1999. The number of students admitted is determined annually by a Decree of the Ministry of University and Research (MUR), taking into account the survey conducted by the University regarding available teaching and clinical resources, as well as the needs expressed by the region and the health service. The MUR will also consider the needs expressed by the region and the health service.
Dublin descriptors
Descriptor 1: Knowledge and understanding
The graduate will be able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the theoretical and practical foundations of logopedics, including the biological, psychological, and social aspects of communication disorders, and the principles of evidence-based practice in rehabilitation.

Descriptor 2: Applying knowledge and understanding
The graduate will be able to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- Conduct comprehensive assessments of communication disorders in diverse populations.
- Develop and implement individualized rehabilitation plans with measurable and achievable goals, adapting to different ages and considering cultural and linguistic differences.
- Monitor and adjust rehabilitation plans based on patient needs.
- Evaluate patient performance in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team.
- Apply research findings to clinical practice.
- Use pedagogical and psychological knowledge to motivate patients and propose effective educational strategies.

Descriptor 3: Making judgments
The graduate will be able to:
- Critically evaluate clinical cases and treatment options.
- Make informed decisions regarding patient care, considering legal, ethical, and patient rights implications.
- Assess the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions.

Descriptor 4: Communication skills
The graduate will be able to:
- Listen, inform, and dialogue with patients and families in an appropriate, effective, and understandable manner.
- Communicate, argue, and justify their actions and decisions with colleagues and different professional figures.
- Adapt communication according to context and respect cultural, ethnic, and value differences of the patients.
- Implement logopedic counseling techniques to activate the client's resources and abilities, involving family and caregivers in the rehabilitation process.
- Use documentation tools for clinical-rehabilitation activities.

Descriptor 5: Learning skills
The graduate will be able to conduct self-assessment of their educational level to maintain their knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice and to plan self-education paths to enhance their competencies, particularly in evidence-based practice in rehabilitation and logopedics. Over three years, they will acquire learning skills and competencies enabling, at the end of the course, the continuation of studies, including a master's degree in Class LM/SNT/02, scientific specialization courses, and advanced permanent and recurring training (1st and 2nd level master's, specialization courses), update and in-depth courses (Continuing Medical Education), with a high degree of autonomy.

Descriptor 6: Professional skills
The graduate will be able to:
- Plan and manage rehabilitation interventions in diverse contexts.
- Work effectively within interdisciplinary teams.
- Maintain professional standards of quality in providing logopedic interventions.
- Document clinical-rehabilitation activities accurately.
- Engage in continuous professional development.

UNIVERSITY: Università degli Studi di Foggia
COURSE: [1686] Speech Therapy
SECTION: Critical Judgment
URL: https://www.unifg.it

The program aims to develop the following competencies:

- To collect, analyze, and interpret significant data regarding patient needs using standardized tools, interviews, and observations.
- To conduct accurate functional assessments, formulating necessary elaborations for drafting an appropriate therapeutic plan (rehabilitative/adaptive; educational/re-educational).
- To define objectives and prognostic hypotheses considering both the extent of damage and potential recovery indicators.
- To plan and implement care and rehabilitation interventions focused on specific functional outcomes through a person-centered approach.
- To carry out interventions safely and effectively, performing periodic checks and modifying the treatment plan as needed.
- To share the therapeutic program with the patient, other individuals, and professionals, establishing the so-called 'therapeutic contract'.
- To evaluate treatment plan results, verifying overall effectiveness based on outcomes and responses to intervention, recording changes, and addressing critical situations.
- To provide specific technical consultation to patients, families, other professionals, or relevant entities.

EDUCATION THERAPEUTIC: The healthcare activity aimed at developing awareness and responsibility in individuals and groups. It represents an integral part of patient care and is realized through therapeutic education interventions, establishing a supportive relationship to assist the patient and family, and helping the person develop self-care and functional recovery skills.

PREVENTION: The Speech Therapist must be able to conduct prevention activities for individuals and the community, in health or with physical and/or mental conditions. This area is an integral part of the therapeutic program, involving activities to identify and overcome risk situations for the individual and community through investigations, screenings, and follow-up. The Speech Therapist must promote actions necessary for maintaining health, overcoming disability, and preventing further disability deterioration. They must identify health and disability prevention needs by recognizing potentially risky situations, particularly through targeted screenings for early detection of language, communication, hearing, and oral function disorders across all age groups.

MANAGEMENT: Includes all management tools (resources, information, economic aspects) essential for the correct daily implementation of the Speech Therapist's work through the following actions:
- Acting according to quality criteria using appropriate tools.
- Managing privacy.
- Managing clinical risk.
- Making decisions after implementing a proper problem-solving process. The Speech Therapist must:
  - Identify the nature of problems, analyze, choose, interpret, and resolve problems, possibly through collaboration.
  - In managing their work, recognize and respect roles and competencies, interact and collaborate with multi-professional teams, and use General Guidelines and protocols to standardize operational methods.
  - In clinical risk management, identify and report difficulties.
  - Utilize information and computer systems to analyze data. This area encompasses all procedures and tools enabling the Speech Therapist to organize their work comprehensively.

TRAINING/AUTOTRAINING: The context in which the Speech Therapist forms, develops, and consolidates their cultural foundations through the following competencies: conducting training programs after performing adequate self-assessment; identifying learning and training objectives in the educational path with coordinator and tutor, and evaluating objective achievement; assuming responsibility for their own training and professional development.

COMMUNICATION AND RELATIONSHIP: Represents the primary dimension of human social life and is fully attributable as an indispensable competence for the healthcare professional. This area defines the relational substrate through which the Speech Therapist will apply their professional practice in the rehabilitative, social, and institutional context, through communication and relationship skills with the user and their family, using active listening and managing relational dynamics, while interacting with other professionals, coordinators, tutors, and operators from other facilities.

Roles President TOMMASO CASSANO Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Nurse Graduates perform their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in the territory and home care, in dependent or self-employed status; they contribute to the training of support staff and directly participate in professional updating.
Final exam characteristics.
The characteristics of the final exam are those indicated in Article 7, paragraph 4 of the Interministerial Decree of 19.02.2009, no. 119 (G.U. 25.05.2009). The Nursing degree is obtained by passing a final exam consisting of the writing and discussion of a written paper on a theoretical-practical topic. It is preceded by a professional exam, enabling for the profession of Nurse, demonstrating skills related to nursing care practice, which can be carried out either at the patient's bedside or as a simulated practical exam. Papers may also be written in a foreign language previously agreed upon. The final exam has the value of State Exam enabling the exercise of the profession.
Access requirements.
Candidates who possess a Secondary School Diploma or equivalent foreign title under Article 6, paragraphs 1 and 2, of D.M. 270/04 and have passed the admission selection test may be admitted to the Nursing Bachelor's Degree Course.
The admission exam takes place according to modalities defined by the Ministry of Education, University and Research, and currently consists of a written test of 60 multiple-choice questions on topics of Logic and General Culture, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics. The selection test is conducted on a single date throughout the national territory and is indicated by the Ministry.
Learning abilities.
Graduates must possess the theoretical and practical abilities necessary for the exercise of the Nurse profession acquired during the training path of the study course.
The acquired abilities must enable the graduate not only to continue and deepen their knowledge in the field of Nursing through updating and continuous training, but also to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy and applicative potential in broader contexts. Such abilities are assessed through in-course tests, thesis writing and final exam.
Communication abilities.
Graduates must be able to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions; fully manage the communication process, fostering the creation of an empathetic and trusting climate with both specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, and possess the ability to adapt their relational style to assistive situations and within the team, according to the situation and needs that arise. These abilities are acquired and verified through meetings with patients, tutors and assistants, promoting active student participation and multidisciplinary team work activities and final reports.

-----

### Summary of the Nursing Degree Program at the University of Foggia (Italy)  

#### **Program Objectives**  
The program trains **registered nurses** (Infermieri) to:  
- Provide **preventive, curative, palliative, and rehabilitative care** across all age groups.  
- Identify health needs of individuals and communities.  
- Plan, manage, and evaluate nursing interventions.  
- Collaborate with healthcare teams and support staff.  
- Apply diagnostic/therapeutic prescriptions and promote health education.  

#### **Admission Process**  
- **Competitive entrance exam** with ranking based on scores.  
- Applicants must specify **three preferred courses** (I, II, III option) and **one campus** (5 campuses total).  
- **Priority** is given to the **first-choice campus**; remaining spots fill via second/third choices.  
- **Non-EU students** have a separate ranking.  
- **Obligatory Academic Requirements (OFA)**:  
  - Students lacking foundational knowledge in **Biology, Physics, and Biochemistry** must complete remedial courses (via e-learning or personalized plans) within the first semester.  
  - OFA can be waived via credit recognition (e.g., prior coursework).  

#### **Curriculum Structure**  
1. **Core Nursing Sciences**:  
   - General, clinical, and pediatric nursing.  
   - Medical-surgical disciplines (pathology, diagnostics, therapy).  
   - Chronic care, maternal-child health, critical care, and disability support.  
2. **Foundational Disciplines**:  
   - Human anatomy, physiology, biomedical sciences.  
   - Sanitary physics, medical statistics, informatics.  
   - Emergency response and first aid.  
3. **Professional Skills**:  
   - **Human sciences & psychopedagogy** (for patient/colleague interaction).  
   - **Public health, prevention, and healthcare services** (including radioprotection).  
   - **Healthcare management** (economics, legal aspects of healthcare).  
4. **Language & Practical Training**:  
   - **English (scientific focus)**.  
   - **Professional labs** (MED/45 discipline).  
   - **Clinical internships** (mandatory for licensure).  
   - **Seminars** on emerging nursing topics.  

#### **Legal Framework**  
- Governed by **Ministerial Decree (D.M. 14/09/1994, n. 739)** and subsequent updates.  
- Graduates are authorized to practice as **nurses** under Italian law.  

#### **Key Features**  
- **No campus transfers** between the 5 locations (Foggia, Bari, etc.) for the same program.  
- **Integrated approach**: Combines technical skills (e.g., diagnostics, therapy), relational competencies, and management.  
- **Focus on modern challenges**: Chronic diseases, critical care, and interdisciplinary teamwork.  

#### **Competencies Expected**  
- **Technical**: Apply medical protocols, use diagnostic tools.  
- **Relational**: Communicate effectively with patients, families, and healthcare teams.  
- **Ethical**: Uphold patient rights and professional ethics.  
- **Adaptive**: Respond to evolving healthcare needs (e.g., public health crises).  

This program prepares graduates for **full licensure** and roles in hospitals, clinics, public health, and community care, emphasizing **holistic, evidence-based nursing practice**.

### **Summary: Bachelor's Program in Dental Hygiene (Igiene Dentale)**  
*Regulated by Law 10 August 2000, n. 251, Article 3, Paragraph 1*  

---

#### **Key Features**  
- **Duration**: 3 years (Bachelor’s degree).  
- **Professional Role**:  
  - Prevents and treats non-surgical periodontal diseases.  
  - Promotes oral health through patient education, lifestyle advice (e.g., oral hygiene, smoking cessation), and motivation.  
  - Works under the supervision of dentists/physicians or independently in modern oral medicine.  
  - *Career Advancement*: Coordination roles possible after completing a Master’s (LM/SNT3 in *Scienze delle professioni sanitarie tecniche assistenziali*).  

---

#### **Admission Requirements**  
1. **Entrance Exam**:  
   - Multiple-choice test on **Logic, General Culture, Biology, Chemistry, Math, Physics**.  
   - **Minimum score**: 20/100.  
2. **Additional Educational Obligation (OFA)**:  
   - If score <30% in any subject, must complete OFA within **Year 1**.  
   - OFA recovery: Written test (50% correct answers required) on the deficient subject.  
   - *Failure to complete OFA blocks enrollment in related courses*.  

---

#### **Curriculum Structure**  
| **Year** | **Focus**                                                                 | **Key Subjects**                                                                 |
|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Year 1** | Basic sciences, medical English, patient interaction, scientific methodology. | Biology, Chemistry, Math, Physics, Medical English, Patient Communication.       |
| **Years 2–3** | Medical/surgical disciplines, specialized dental hygiene, clinical internships. | Periodontology, Oral Pathology, Pharmacology, Clinical Practice, Soft Skills.    |

---

#### **Core Competencies**  
- **Biomedical Knowledge**: Anatomy, physiology, pathology (oral/dental diseases across age groups).  
- **Technical Skills**: Prevention, diagnosis, documentation of oral diseases.  
- **Communication**: Patient education, motivation, and improving compliance.  
- **Professional Skills**:  
  - Use of EU languages (e.g., English) for scientific exchange.  
  - Continuous learning via bibliographic resources.  
  - Integration with broader healthcare contexts (e.g., systemic diseases, pharmacology).  

---

#### **Work Context**  
- **Primary Duties**:  
  - Non-surgical periodontal treatment.  
  - Promoting oral health through preventive strategies.  
  - Adapting care for medically compromised patients (e.g., elderly, disabilities).  
- **Team Collaboration**: Works alongside dentists/physicians; may coordinate teams post-Master’s.  

---

#### **Progression Pathway**  
- **Bachelor’s → Master’s (LM/SNT3)**: Enables advanced roles (e.g., team coordination, specialized care).  
- **Legal Framework**: Directly aligned with Italian healthcare regulations for dental hygiene professionals.  

---

**Note**: The program emphasizes **clinical practice** (internships) and **patient-centered care**, preparing graduates for direct roles in dental clinics, public health, and preventive programs.  
*For details on OFA recovery or curriculum specifics, consult the university’s official program guidelines.* 🌟

Roles President RAFFAELE IVAN CINCIONE Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
DIETITIAN The Dietetics graduate can perform professional and/or dietary-nutritional consulting tasks within:
- Public or private healthcare institutions;
- Public or private collective catering services and catering services.
The professional contribution of the Dietetics graduate is also required in companies operating in the agri-food chain.
Dietitians are also required in companies involved at various levels in thermal and aesthetic medicine.
Final exam characteristics.
The characteristics of the final exam are those indicated in Article 7, paragraph 4 of the Interministerial Decree of February 19, 2009, no. 119 (G.U. May 25, 2009). The Dietetics degree is obtained by passing a final exam consisting of the writing and discussion of a written paper on a theoretical-practical topic. It is preceded by a professional exam, enabling the profession of Dietitian, demonstrating practical skills in a simulated clinical practice. The papers may also be written in a foreign language previously agreed upon. The final exam has the value of a State Exam enabling the professional practice.
Required knowledge for access.
Candidates who possess a Secondary School Diploma or an equivalent foreign title under Article 6, paragraph 1 of Ministerial Decree No. 270 of October 22, 2004, may be admitted to the Dietetics Bachelor's Degree Course (CdL). Admission to the Dietetics CdL takes place according to procedures defined by MIUR and, to date, consists of a written test (multiple-choice quiz) covering topics in Logic and General Culture, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics.
The Bachelor's Degree Course requires verification of adequate initial preparation.
In case of negative verification, the student is assigned specific additional educational obligations (OFA) according to the detailed procedures set forth in the Course Study Regulations.

-----

**Program Overview**  
The Bachelor’s Degree in Dietetics (Laurea in Dietistica) is designed to train professionals qualified to practice as Dietitians, focusing on the theoretical and practical study of dietetics, nutrition, and health. The program emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration, evidence-based practice, and the application of scientific knowledge to promote health and manage nutritional needs across diverse populations. It integrates clinical, public health, and managerial competencies to prepare graduates for roles in healthcare, community nutrition, and food service management.

---

**Core Competencies**  
Graduates are equipped to:  
- Assess nutritional needs for healthy individuals and those with medical conditions (e.g., age, sex, physiological states, diseases).  
- Evaluate nutritional status using dietary intake analysis, body composition assessment, and energy expenditure measurements.  
- Develop, implement, and monitor medical diets and artificial nutrition plans (hospitalized or home-based).  
- Collaborate in multidisciplinary teams for treating eating disorders and managing chronic diseases.  
- Design and manage community and institutional food services (e.g., hospitals, schools, elderly care).  
- Conduct nutritional education and health promotion programs for individuals and populations.  
- Participate in research and innovation in dietetic-nutritional science.  
- Communicate effectively with patients, healthcare professionals, and stakeholders while adhering to ethical standards.  

---

**Curriculum Structure**  
The program is structured around three pillars:  
1. **Foundational Sciences**:  
   - Human anatomy, physiology, biomedical sciences, medical physics, statistics, and IT.  
   - Emergency response and first aid protocols.  
2. **Clinical and Applied Dietetics**:  
   - Specialized disciplines: Endocrinology, gastroenterology, internal medicine, pediatrics, food science, and food technology.  
   - Clinical nutrition, diet planning, and artificial nutrition.  
3. **Professional and Soft Skills**:  
   - Human sciences and psychopedagogy for effective patient and team communication.  
   - Public health, prevention, and health services management (including radioprotection).  
   - Healthcare economics, health law, and English for scientific communication.  
   - Practical training (professional internship) in clinical, community, and food service settings.  

---

**Work Context**  
Graduates work in:  
- **Healthcare Settings**: Hospitals, clinics, and private practices (as employees or freelancers).  
- **Community and Public Health**: Schools, elderly care facilities, and public health programs.  
- **Food Service Management**: Designing menus, managing institutional catering, and collaborating with hygiene-sanitation authorities.  
- **Education and Research**: Developing nutritional guidelines, conducting studies, and training healthcare teams.  

---

**Additional Components**  
- **Professional Internship**: Mandatory practical training in clinical, community, and food service environments.  
- **Language Skills**: Scientific English for accessing global research and collaborating internationally.  
- **Interdisciplinary Focus**: Integration of medical, managerial, and communication skills to address complex health challenges.  
- **Admission Process**: Competitive selection with preference for three program choices (I, II, III), including separate rankings for non-EU students.  

---

**Program Distinction**  
This curriculum stands out for its holistic approach, balancing clinical expertise with public health and management skills, ensuring graduates are adaptable to evolving healthcare demands and capable of contributing to both individual and population-level health outcomes.

Role of the professional The degree enables the holder to practice as a physiotherapist within the National Health Service (NHS) and other healthcare settings, providing rehabilitation services to patients across all age groups. The physiotherapist will work collaboratively with other healthcare professionals to develop and implement individualized rehabilitation plans, utilizing evidence-based practice principles. The physiotherapist will be responsible for conducting assessments, designing treatment plans, and evaluating outcomes, while maintaining professional standards and ethical conduct.

Final exam requirements The final exam consists of a written test and an oral examination. The written test assesses theoretical knowledge and critical analysis skills. The oral examination evaluates the student's ability to apply knowledge to clinical scenarios, communicate effectively, and demonstrate professional judgment. The final grade is determined by the combined results of both components.

Admission requirements The admission requirements include a high school diploma or equivalent qualification. Candidates must demonstrate sufficient knowledge in biology, chemistry, and physics. For candidates who do not meet the minimum score in the admission test, additional educational obligations (OFA) must be fulfilled during the first year of study, as specified in the Course Didactic Regulations.

Learning outcomes The physiotherapy graduate will be able to conduct self-assessment of their educational level to maintain the highest professional standards and design self-education paths to enhance their competencies, particularly in Evidence Based Practice within rehabilitation and physiotherapy. Over the three years, students will develop learning abilities and competencies enabling them to pursue further studies, including a master's degree in Class LM/SNT/02, scientific specialization courses, and continuing education programs (1st and 2nd level master's, specialization courses), with a high degree of autonomy. These abilities will be developed and verified through exam preparation, internship attendance and evaluation (combining theory and practice), critical use of scientific literature, and preparation for the final exam.

Teaching tools: classroom activities, seminars, simulation laboratories, internship.

Communication skills The graduate must be able to manage communication effectively as both a competency in communication, emotional, and relational skills, facilitating daily physiotherapy practice for individual patient benefit, and as the ability to establish a meaningful therapeutic relationship with the person and an effective relationship with all other professionals in the same or other disciplines. They must be able to use healthcare communication tools, demonstrating the ability to complete physiotherapy records, draft therapeutic reports, design physiotherapy interventions, etc., communicating clearly, concisely, and professionally in both verbal and written form, technically and grammatically accurate, and capable of translating technical language into understandable terms for non-specialists. They must be able to communicate appropriately in international scientific contexts to convey ideas, problems, and solutions. These skills will be acquired and verified through patient encounters, tutor and assistant meetings, promoting active student participation, through multidisciplinary team activities, and final reports.
